scan060.normalisation: candidate lines only; address column dropped; PC-relative targets '@(<hex> <SYM>)' reduced to '@(<SYM>)'; sorted. A newer scan060.py cannot move the gate: the set is pinned by this sha.
scan060.why: The 55 inherited candidates are stock movep/cas2/cmp2/64-bit-mul sites in stock and FPSP code that candidate-3 already carries to a real 060. They are not a driver-line finding. If one is ever shown to execute on silicon, that is a port-lane issue (Antti), not a gate change.

scan060_tables.why: KT-31: amix-040-060-port tools/scan060-tables.py (6e8f973) -- a scan060 MOVEP candidate inside a gcc switch dispatch table (movew %pc@(T,%dN:l:2),%d0 / jmp %pc@(T,%d0:w), bound from the moveq before it) is a misdecoded 16-bit offset, not an instruction. KD060-ZI's one: ide_040.o idequeue's 54-entry table, the entry at +0x1616 decodes as `movepw %d0,%a2@(1152)` (.text+0xfd656 in the chain). Reader sha pinned: a newer reader cannot move the gate; anything else new stays a failure.
